records.not_understood: The 93.9 percent residual is the single largest not-understood in this program, and this draft names it rather than smoothing it over. The program does not know why the compilations disagree: candidate causes include how each compilation segments texts into signs, the crosswalk itself (of 762 sign pairs, 383 are conflict pairs, where the sources map signs differently), and differences in which objects each compilation includes. Until the residual is attributed, every positional claim in this program that rests on one compilation carries an unmeasured cross-compilation risk. What would change the picture: a matched-object study on inscriptions both compilations record, comparing sign by sign on the same physical objects - Phase-131's first arm found zero shared object keys to join on, which is itself part of the problem.

explanation_record.explanation_text: The check compared the compilations sign by sign through the program's crosswalk (Phase-125). The result was a frozen-rule failure, recorded as FAIL - DISAGREEMENT. First, most signs could not be judged at all: of 286 sign pairs, only 16 had enough occurrences in both compilations to pass the count floor fixed in advance; 270 fell below it. Among the 16 judgeable pairs, the typical positional profile differed by a distance of 0.637 (median TV distance, where 0 is identical and 1 is completely different). Two follow-ups kept the failure honest. Phase-127 asked whether small samples explain the gap: sampling noise alone, measured inside one compilation at the same token counts, produces a typical distance of only 0.083 - so the disagreement is not a sampling artefact (0 of 999 trials reached it). Phase-131 then tried to attribute the disagreement to named causes - segmentation differences, sign substitutions, corpus composition - and could attribute only 6.1 percent of it. The remaining 93.9 percent is residual: present, measured, and unexplained. Under the tightened framework (Spec 026) all three phases were replayed exactly and reproduced, so the numbers stand; what they mean is the open part.

The pilot (Phase-132) measured exact-sequence agreement of 0.20 against the frozen floor of 0.80, and the release gates all failed; the dataset was not published, and the line was closed. The Spec 026 rerun (Phase-383) then put a proper interval on the pilot's number: the bootstrap confidence interval for agreement is [0.10, 0.32], far below the floor - the bounded claim is not merely unproven, it is contradicted for this coding basis at this protocol. The record also carries a disclosure that must stay attached to any retelling: every coder in these passes was an AI agent of a single model family. The failure is therefore a failure of one origin group's coding, measured honestly; it is not evidence about what trained human epigraphers would do, and the two motif pilots run on a similar basis (Phases 134 and 135) separately closed as inconclusive, in the middle band - they neither rescue nor worsen this verdict.

explanation_record.explanation_text: The check (Phase-136) used a within-site stratified test (Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel) on 2,195 inscriptions whose final sign could be mapped, drawn from 2,676 seals and tablets. The statistic came out at 47.0047; a permutation check - shuffling the labels 9,999 times to see how often chance alone produces a gap this large - never reached it (p = 0.0001, the smallest value the run could report). The size of the difference: the odds of a TERMINAL14 ending are about 2.38 times higher on one object type than the other (odds ratio 2.384, confidence interval 1.847 to 3.077). After the family correction across the three Spec 024 tests (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05), the adjusted value is q = 0.00015 - comfortably inside. A later leave-one-site-out pass (Phase-141) found the result stable when any single site is removed. The boundaries matter as much as the numbers: 49.0 percent of the lineage layer's rows could not be joined to the catalogue at all, so the result describes the joined subset of one corpus lineage (the horus84 ICIT-lineage layer), not the Indus corpus in general - the report itself insists on that wording, and so does this draft.

explanation_record.explanation_text: The first check (Phase-137) found nothing: the association statistic (chi-square 745.95) was the kind of value chance produces routinely - a permutation test returned p = 0.7354, so the verdict at the time was NOT SUPPORTED. The Spec 026 rerun (Phase-384) sharpened the question into the bounded form the program now uses: is the effect at least as large as the practical margin fixed in advance (an effect size of 0.10, where the descriptive value in this layer had been 0.1154)? The rerun's answer, from an interval estimate that passed its own validity control (an earlier version of the interval was invalid and the program caught and discarded it - that self-catch is part of the record), puts the effect between 0.059 and 0.078 - entirely below the 0.10 margin. The bounded claim is therefore recorded as CONTRADICTED at the declared margin: there may be a small site effect in this layer, but not one as large as the claim required. Note what this verdict is about - the Holdat layer only. The same question in the ICIT-lineage layer (the F3 claim) came out the other way, and that disagreement between layers is itself unexplained (see the F3 draft).

explanation_record.author: Tristen Pierson
explanation_record.ai_assistance_disclosure: Drafted in full by an AI agent (Muse Spark, via Muse) on 2026-10-13, at the direction of Tristen Pierson. The drafting AI is not the author (OD-2).
explanation_record.explanation_text: The check (Phase-137) found a strong association: chi-square 4966.36, an effect size (Cramer's V - a 0-to-1 scale for how strongly two things go together) of 0.2190, and a permutation p of 0.0001 - chance alone essentially never produces a gap this large. The Spec 026 rerun (Phase-384) confirmed the bounded form: the effect's interval [0.182, 0.210] lies entirely above the practical floor, so SUPPORTED stands. Now the conditions, which the program has attached to this result from the start and which this draft repeats because they are part of the result: the sites in this corpus differ in their period mix, in how well their objects survived, and in their excavation history - the confounders named in Spec 024 section 5.1, alongside text-type and text-length mix. An association with 'site' can be those differences wearing a site label. And the corpus is one lineage - the ICIT line, through the horus84 layer - while the same test in the Holdat layer found no effect of the required size (the F2 claim). One more fact that belongs here: when the follow-up study (Spec 025, the G1 claim) controlled for composition and preservation, the association survived - but chronology, the period mix, was not controlled there either.

explanation_record.explanation_text: The check (Phase-140) re-ran the F3 test with the shuffling done inside groups matched for composition and preservation (preservation was recorded for 99.9 percent of the rows, which is what made the control possible). The observed statistic, 4966.36, stood far above the shuffled values (typical value 2684.74); not one of 9,999 shuffles reached it (p = 0.0001). The Spec 026 rerun (Phase-385) confirmed the effect size: the interval [0.184, 0.210] lies entirely above the declared margin, so SUPPORTED under control stands. The rider, which the program requires wherever this result is stated and which this draft states in the body, not a footnote: chronology is not controlled in the primary test. Sites' period mixes differ, and until period is held fixed the same way, part of what is called a site effect may be a time effect - later and earlier cities are not the same cities. A chronology sensitivity bound is reported alongside the result, but it is not the controlled verdict.

records.not_understood: The jackknife failure is the not-understood core: the program cannot tell whether Harappa carries the signal because Harappa is genuinely central, or because its corpus is so much larger than the others that it dominates any pooled measure. A 1.7-percent association also cannot carry a movement story by itself - shared period, shared trade goods and shared excavation practices all predict the same small resemblance. Stage 2 of the movement study was not executed as a stage, and the timing question behind it (Q6) remains not-yet-testable even after the chronology-spine extension (Spec 030, Phase-394) closed negative. What would change the picture: the Harappa-specific follow-up arms (Spec 028, drafted alongside this one) are the program's own answer to the jackknife problem - and both came back inconclusive as well, which is itself the current state of knowledge.

explanation_record.explanation_text: The primary result: site similarity accounts for a small share of the differences between repertoires - median adjusted R-squared 0.01677, that is about 1.7 percent of the variation, with interval [0.01032, 0.02397]. The signal is consistent (the rejection share was 1.000, and both controls passed: the negative control sat near zero, the positive control behaved as designed). But the frozen SUPPORTED rule also required the result to survive leaving any one site out, and removing Harappa dropped the median to 0.00928 - below the 0.01 margin fixed in advance. The CONTRADICTED rule did not fire either. The verdict is therefore INCONCLUSIVE, exactly as the frozen rules produce it. A sensitivity version restricted to complete cases read slightly higher (0.01793) and carried no verdict. The study's own record also notes what could not be run at all: the planned Parpola-numbering sensitivity was not estimable, because the crosswalk covers only 17.57 percent of the relevant signs.

explanation_record.explanation_text: The audit (Spec 026) inventoried 116 items from that history and reclassified each under the tightened framework: 8 items required full reruns, 12 were reproduce-only, 61 reinterpret-only, 27 unaffected, and 8 not rerunnable. For 75 of the 116, the evidentiary status changed - not because the old arithmetic was wrong, but because the old labels claimed more than the old checks could carry. The four reruns show the range: the keyed-transcription claim was contradicted (Phase-383); the Holdat site claim was contradicted at its declared margin while the ICIT site claim stood (Phase-384); the controlled site claim stood at its margin (Phase-385); and the cross-compilation line (Phases 116, 125, 127, 131) replayed exactly, its uncomfortable numbers reproduced rather than revised away (Phase-386). The assessments are appended historical assessments: the original result files and ledger entries were never rewritten, and the new readings sit alongside the old labels so the change is itself inspectable.
